title: Trauma camera shake with seeded gradient noise
purpose: Shake a three.js camera after hits and explosions: trauma in [0, 1] decays linearly, and the shake is trauma to a power times seeded smooth gradient noise on three translation and three rotation channels, applied around a base pose that the shake never changes. Deterministic for a seed and time.

engine.name: node
engine.notes: Pure ES2020, also runs in any browser; applyTo poses a three.js camera through position.set and quaternion.set. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run.

exports.name: CameraShake
exports.signature: new CameraShake(options = {}); addTrauma(amount) -> trauma; update(deltaSeconds) -> trauma; sample(time = this.time) -> {translation, rotation, intensity}; applyTo(camera, basePosition, baseQuaternion = [0, 0, 0, 1]) -> camera
exports.summary: A shake with its own trauma and clock that poses any object with position.set and quaternion.set around a base pose.

exports.name: shakeOffsets
exports.signature: shakeOffsets(trauma, time, options = {}) -> {translation: [x, y, z], rotation: [pitch, yaw, roll], intensity}
exports.summary: The shake at a time for a trauma level; intensity = clamp(trauma, 0, 1)^exponent.

exports.name: shakeNoise
exports.summary: Seeded 1D gradient noise: zero on integers, quintic fade, the same on every platform.

exports.name: traumaAfter
exports.summary: Trauma left after linear decay, never below zero.

options.name: exponent
options.meaning: Shake intensity is trauma to this power, so small hits stay subtle.

options.name: frequency
options.meaning: How fast the shake changes direction.

options.name: translation
options.meaning: Largest offsets along the camera's right, up and back axes at full trauma.

options.name: rotation
options.meaning: Largest pitch, yaw and roll at full trauma.

options.name: seed
options.meaning: Noise seed; two shakes with different seeds move differently.

limits: A procedural game-feel effect, not a model of a physical camera mount: no inertia, spring or directional response to where the hit came from. The noise is 1D gradient noise, not band-limited, so very high frequencies alias at low frame rates. Translation is applied along the camera's own axes and rotation after the base orientation; the shake does not avoid walls or clipping. Trauma decays linearly; an exponential decay needs a different update. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2; frame-time behaviour was not measured.
technique_references: 1D gradient noise with integer lattice hashing and a quintic fade
Quaternion composition of a base orientation with Euler offsets
